reason: Remove boundary limits from Dockside mobile thread navigation. When the queue reaches the last thread, next arrow or left swipe wraps to the first thread; when at the first thread, previous arrow or right swipe wraps to the last thread. Keep singleton queues disabled and preserve the current active/unread ordering.
spec:
# Dockside Mobile Thread Navigation

## Request

> Make a bb plugin for bb mobile to have like arrows or tinder stylrer to go strong it the threads more easily. You teasesrch and do it don’t ask me

## Goal

Extend Dockside with one-thumb mobile navigation across active and unread
threads in every project through previous/next controls and horizontal swipes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [AC-1] The current thread plus visible, non-archived active and unread threads across every project are ordered by latest attention with deterministic fallbacks.
- [ ] [AC-UI-1] [UI] At widths up to 767px, a compact strip above the composer offers accessible 44px previous/next arrows, title and position. Desktop is unchanged.
- [ ] [AC-UI-3] [UI] The strip shows the current thread's live BB status using the host-provided accessible indicator label, with "Idle" when the host reports no indicator. Status changes update without navigation or message inspection.
- [ ] [AC-UI-2] [UI] A deliberate horizontal swipe on the strip changes one thread; vertical movement, cancellation, short gestures and gestures outside the strip never navigate.
- [ ] [AC-2] Boundaries disable navigation without wrapping. Loading, errors and singleton lists are safe; stale requests cannot change the current thread.
- [ ] [AC-UI-4] [UI] Every queued thread shows its project initial using Dockside's effective project color, including custom colors synchronized through Dockside settings.
- [ ] [AC-3] Dockside owns the implementation, tests and documentation. The standalone Thread Mobile package and root catalog entry are removed.
- [ ] [AC-4] The existing Dockside v0.1.5 installation is removed, the local
  v0.1.6 build is installed and running, and the immutable `dockside/v0.1.6`
  Git release is created from the verified commit and pushed.

## Scope
Dockside app registration, mobile navigation components and helpers, Dockside
project color hook, focused tests and documentation, root catalog/lockfile
cleanup, local replacement install, immutable v0.1.6 tag/release, and live
mobile browser verification.

## Non-goals
No archive/delete/vote gesture, no native BB patch, no desktop UI replacement,
no message-content capture, no inferred completion state, and no second
standalone mobile-navigation plugin.

## Risks
Mobile composer layouts and SDK mounting support must be verified. Gestures
must not steal vertical scrolling or native edge-back gestures. Thread changes
must use native navigation so drafts remain host-owned.

## Verification
Pure tests for ordering/boundaries and gesture classification, SDK typecheck,
plugin build, root checks subject to full-suite approval rules, local install
and reload, installed-source/status inspection, exact release-tag commit
inspection, and Steel mobile/desktop screenshot and interaction checks.

## Capability Deltas

See deltas/mobile-thread-navigation.md.

deltas.purpose:
Give mobile BB users a fast, safe way to move between eligible threads without
leaving the conversation surface.

### Requirement: Mobile threads support bounded one-thumb navigation
Dockside MUST show mobile previous/next controls and a swipeable title above
the current thread composer. It MUST use native thread navigation, include the
current thread plus visible non-archived active and unread threads from every
project, and order them by latest attention with deterministic fallbacks.

#### Scenario: User browses active work across projects
- **Given** three eligible threads from multiple projects and the middle thread open on mobile
- **When** the user taps next or deliberately swipes left on the strip
- **Then** the next thread opens exactly once through host navigation
- **And** the final thread disables next instead of wrapping

### Requirement: Project context uses Dockside's effective color
Each eligible thread MUST show a compact project initial beside its title.
The badge MUST use the same automatic or custom effective project color as
Dockside and update when Dockside's synchronized color setting changes.

#### Scenario: User customizes a project color
- **Given** a project has a custom color in Dockside settings
- **When** one of its threads appears in the mobile navigation queue
- **Then** its project badge uses that custom color and a readable foreground

### Requirement: Gestures preserve ordinary conversation interaction
Only horizontal gestures beginning on the strip title MUST navigate.
Vertical, short, cancelled and multi-touch gestures MUST not navigate.
Desktop MUST retain its normal layout without the strip.

#### Scenario: User reads a long response
- **Given** a mobile thread is open
- **When** the user scrolls the conversation or vertically drags the strip
- **Then** no thread navigation occurs

### Requirement: Unavailable lists fail safely
Loading and failed requests MUST disable navigation. Results for old thread
identities MUST be discarded. The plugin MUST not mutate thread content,
archive state or project configuration.

#### Scenario: A request fails
- **Given** a thread list request fails
- **When** the strip renders
- **Then** both navigation arrows are disabled and a retry is available

### Requirement: Current thread status uses live host semantics
The strip MUST show the current thread's host-provided accessible indicator
label. When BB reports no indicator, it MUST show "Idle". The plugin MUST NOT
infer status from message text, timestamps, or thread titles.

#### Scenario: Thread begins or finishes work
- **Given** the current thread is visible in BB's live sidebar projection
- **When** BB changes its indicator or accessible indicator label
- **Then** Thread Glide updates the compact status without navigating
- **And** the status remains distinguishable from the numeric thread position

### Requirement: Dockside mobile navigation is released immutably
The verified Dockside package MUST be installable as version 0.1.6 and the
`dockside/v0.1.6` tag MUST identify the exact reviewed release commit.

#### Scenario: User installs the new Dockside release
- **Given** Dockside v0.1.5 is currently installed
- **When** it is replaced with the verified v0.1.6 package
- **Then** Dockside v0.1.6 is running with the mobile navigation bundle
- **And** the pushed release tag identifies that exact source commit
